description: 47 climate solutions ranked by potential gain per initial effort. Chain per solution: reduction potential at full deployment (gigatonne CO2eq per year) times the effective years of the period 2025 to 2050 gives the avoided emissions; times the social cost of carbon (Rennert et al. 2022, converted to EUR) gives the gain in trillion EUR; times the welfare cost of carbon (Bressler 2021 mortality cost, times life years lost per death, times the Maslow extension to the two lowest need levels) gives the gain in billion htp; divided by the initial effort in person years gives the ratio the solutions are sorted by. Potentials are gross and not additive: instruments and the hardware they finance avoid the same tonnes. Anchors with a source: coal and total fossil CO2 (Global Carbon Budget 2024), methane (UNEP CCAC 2021 with IPCC AR6 GWP100), solar and wind ranges (IPCC AR6 WG3), the 2030 potentials of efficiency, buildings, transport, materials and food (IPCC AR6 WG3 Figure SPM.7), fossil fuel price reform (IMF 2023). Every other potential and every effort is assumed with its own confidence.

formulas.name: USD to EUR per tonne
formulas.expression: "EUR per tonne" = "USD per tonne" / "USD per EUR"
formulas.latex: \text{EUR per tonne} = \frac{\text{USD per tonne}}{\text{USD per EUR}}

formulas.name: health cost of carbon formula
formulas.expression: "DALY per tonne" = "death per tonne" * "year per death"
formulas.latex: \text{DALY per tonne} = \text{death per tonne} \cdot \text{year per death}

formulas.name: methane to CO2 equivalent
formulas.expression: "gigatonne CO2eq per year" = "megatonne per year" * "global warming potential" / 1000
formulas.latex: \text{gigatonne CO2eq per year} = \frac{\text{megatonne per year} \cdot \text{global warming potential}}{1000}
